# A stash cannot take revealed plaintext along (gitignored), and a pop runs the
# drivers without MERGE_HEAD, so no finalize. Nothing breaks, but a stash is only
# half a stash here - pinned down below.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp wip.txt $TMPDIR/wip.txt
cp other.txt $TMPDIR/other.txt
cp merged.txt $TMPDIR/merged.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

# Edit and seal, but do not commit: the tracked object is dirty.
cp $TMPDIR/wip.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git status --short
stdout '\.sesam/objects/s\.sesam'

exec git stash

# CAVEAT: the stash parked the OBJECT, but the revealed plaintext is gitignored
# and stays behind. The worktree is not clean in sesam terms - the plaintext still
# holds the work that was supposedly stashed away.
exec cat s
stdout 'WIP'
exec sesam status
stdout 'out of sync'

# Commit a different change to the same secret, so the pop has to three-way.
cp $TMPDIR/other.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'other change'

# The pop runs both drivers. The secret conflict lands as markers in the revealed
# file, exactly as it would in a merge.
! exec git stash pop
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file s; 1 conflict'
grep '^<<<<<<< ' s
exec sesam status
stdout 'conflicted'
stdout 'in progress'

# CAVEAT: the audit-log driver ran too, so a stash pop leaves a semantically
# merged log (with a merge entry) staged - a change the user never asked for.
exec git status --short
stdout 'M  \.sesam/audit/log\.jsonl'
stdout 'UU \.sesam/objects/s\.sesam'

# The committed object is untouched (ours) and git keeps the stash entry, so the
# stashed work is still recoverable.
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'OTHER'
exec git stash list
stdout 'stash@\{0\}'

# Resolving is the same as anywhere else: fix the revealed file, seal, add.
cp $TMPDIR/merged.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'MERGED'

# The repo is consistent again and nothing is left in progress.
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec sesam status
! stdout 'in progress'
exec git commit -m 'resolve stash pop'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

-- base.txt --
line one
line two
line three
-- wip.txt --
line one
WIP
line three
-- other.txt --
line one
OTHER
line three
-- merged.txt --
line one
MERGED
line three
